page: Amazon Web Services m6g.large is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration supplies 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs with 1 thread per core) and 8.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The architecture includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions but lacks AVX extensions. Local storage is not provided, requiring network-attached storage via EBS, and network capacity is provisioned at a baseline of 1 Gbps with no bundled public IPv4 addresses or GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight entry-tier compute characteristics aligned with its dual-core Graviton footprint. Single-core performance evaluated via stress-ng registers at 1519.29, placing the instance within the average middle 50% percentile, while multi-core stress-ng reaches 3012.97. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 948.0 and a multi-core score of 1730.0. Large-block memory transfers indicate read speeds of 36.2 GB/sec and write speeds of 18.38 GB/sec. Application-level tests demonstrate 2.29 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 2.35 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The use of dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading provides stable, non-contended execution profiles for baseline services. However, memory bandwidth, compilation performance, and raw parallel compute are bounded by the low core count. The instance is suitable for arm64-compatible workloads that do not demand extensive storage throughput or heavy vector math, including small web servers, microservices, staging environments, light database caching nodes, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.large is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an ARM Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) paired with 8.0 GB of memory, preserving a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. The configuration omits integrated local storage and GPU hardware, relying on external network storage and providing a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance testing shows moderate single-thread compute with a stress-ng score of 1519.29, while multi-threaded benchmarks reflect the limits of its two execution cores, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1730.0 and uncached memory reads of 36.2 GB/sec. Because each vCPU operates as an independent physical core without hyperthreading, the instance ensures predictable execution timing for arm64-compiled workloads. It is positioned for lightweight web application serving, backend microservices, development infrastructure, and small-scale caching layers.
